# no-trailing-punctuation

- ID: `MD026`
- Category: Headings
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `headings`

Headings do not end with a period, comma, semicolon, colon or exclamation mark.

## Why

Headings are not full sentences, so they need no closing punctuation.

## Options

Set them under `rules.no-trailing-punctuation.options`.

- `punctuation` (`string`, default `.,;:!。，；：！`): Characters that a heading may
  not end with.

## Fix

The fix deletes the trailing punctuation. gomdlint reports a heading without a
fix when the deletion would leave it showing nothing. It does the same when the
document may link to heading anchors, because the fix may change the heading's
anchor. gomdlint may report a finding without a fix when the fix would change a
line with one character in brackets, such as \[x\] or \[1\], or the lines around
it up to a blank line, because it could add or remove a task list checkbox.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

## Install:

Run the installer.
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:11 Heading ends with trailing punctuation ":"
```

The fix changes it to:

```markdown
# Guide

## Install

Run the installer.
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  no-trailing-punctuation:
    options:
      punctuation: .,;:!。，；：！
```

Under `rules`, `no-trailing-punctuation: false` turns the rule off and
`no-trailing-punctuation: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable no-trailing-punctuation` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line no-trailing-punctuation -->
```
